description:
Milo is a malted drink from Australia, it's supposed to be chocolate but it doesn't taste of chocolate at all. 
It's pretty popular around the world so I thought I would make a really good ice cream base with it, it's so good, you can include add ins and go to town. 

What will you need to make it:

450g Milk @ 2% fat
550g Cream @ 33% fat
170g Sugar
90g Milo
30g SMP
2g Stabiliser

Make sure to keep the heat at around 80C for 20 mins though as you need to evaporate some of the water to make this super smooth.

comments.text: How much sugar would you recommend that I can reduce for this recipe?

comments.text: If you desperately want to take some out, use 140-150g. It will freeze hard and will have some ice.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: @PolarIceCreamery  Can I replace it with dextrose then?
comments.author: @fransiscawong9714

comments.text: @fransiscawong9714   dextrose and sucrose are not interchangable. Why do you want to? Are you looking to reduce the amount of sugar overall or what?
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: @PolarIceCreamery  More on the taste I guess so not really looking to reduce the sugar overall just the sweetness level.
comments.author: @fransiscawong9714

comments.text: @fransiscawong9714   ah in which case, drop the sugar to 100g and add 45g of dextrose. That will reduce the sweetness by 20%.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: @PolarIceCreamery  Thankyou!🥰
comments.author: @fransiscawong9714

comments.text: Which stabiliser I should use ?
comments.author: @user-he5uf8eg7z

comments.text: You can use, xanthan gum, guar gum etc. The list of options is pretty big. Maybe check out the stabilizer videos as I go through a good few of them.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: I made this again today, substituting Milo with Horlicks, to try and produce a Malteasers flavour. The key for me was adding salt - both to the base, and to the chocolate that I melted and then drizzled into the machine while churning. Just a few pinches, I kept tasting until it was just right. This one came out even better than the previous one, and so accurate! Salt! (Btw I add a pinch to almost all flavours, it adds extra depth always)
comments.author: @shvekal

comments.text: It certainly does help boost complex flavors. A lot of folk don’t like adding it but I do it personally.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: Made this substituting Milo (not available here) with Horlicks, and realised I could turn it into sort of a Malteasers ice cream with a bit of milk chocolate, so that's what I did. Drizzled in some melted milk chocolate and this ice cream turned out brilliant!! Your tip on adding some coconut oil to the melted chocolate makes all the difference (I used to not like the texture that I got from frozen chocolate). Thank you so much for all this delicious ice cream!
comments.author: @shvekal

comments.text: Oh that sounds delicious!! Can I use it in a video?
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: @PolarIceCreamery  Of course! It would be an honour. I think adding some crunch to it would add even more depth and texture. I'm not sure chopped Malteasers would do the trick because of the frozen chocolate bit. I've been looking into making the crunchy part at home but haven't had the time to actually try, so looking forward to your video :D.
